answer: The hydrologist reads the meltwater gauge every day, and the flow of the stream is written down beside the weather for that day. A ferrous flow claimed as measured fails the gauge: the water must have run past the weir at the atlas of the day, and a flow never measured has no litres to count. Faking a season of flows means hiring a reader, forging a hundred daily entries and paying 11,900, while the basalt gauge is checked against the rain records, so a flow whose reading was never taken dries up in the book.
